slides.title: Process & Its States
content: A process is a program in execution that uses system resources like CPU, memory, and I/O devices to perform tasks
A process in memory consists of text segment (code), data segment (global variables), heap (dynamic memory), and stack (function calls)
Process states include new, ready, running, waiting (blocked), suspended, and terminated during its lifecycle
The operating system manages transitions between states using scheduling and resource allocation

slides.title: Process State Transitions
content: A process moves from new to ready when it is created and prepared for execution
It moves from ready to running when the CPU scheduler assigns it CPU time
Running processes move to waiting when they request I/O or resources
Waiting processes return to ready after I/O completion, and running processes terminate after execution
Suspended state occurs when a process is temporarily swapped out of memory to manage resources

slides.title: Process Control Block (PCB)
content: A Process Control Block (PCB) is a data structure that stores all information required to manage a process
It includes process state, process ID (PID), program counter, CPU registers, and memory management details
It also stores scheduling information like priority, CPU usage, and I/O status of the process
PCB enables process scheduling, context switching, resource allocation, and error handling in the operating system

slides.title: Context Switching
content: Context switching is the process where the CPU switches from one process to another to enable multitasking
The OS saves the current process state into its PCB and loads the next process state from its PCB
It is triggered by interrupts, system calls, or scheduling decisions
It ensures efficient CPU utilization and fairness but introduces overhead and performance cost

slides.title: Kernel Mode vs User Mode
content: User mode is where applications run with limited access to system resources for security and stability
Kernel mode is where the operating system runs with full access to hardware and critical resources
System calls, interrupts, and faults cause transitions from user mode to kernel mode
Errors in user mode affect only applications, while errors in kernel mode can crash the entire system

slides.title: Threads (ULT & KLT)
content: A thread is the smallest unit of execution within a process that shares memory but runs independently
User-Level Threads (ULTs) are managed by user libraries, are faster, but can block the entire process
Kernel-Level Threads (KLTs) are managed by the OS, allow true parallelism, and run on multiple CPU cores
Threads improve performance, responsiveness, and resource utilization in modern applications
